question.text: Regulation 91E of LODR read with SEBI's framework requires that the Annual Impact Report (AIR) of a Social Enterprise which has raised funds on SSE shall cover at least what proportion of the program expenditure of the previous financial year?

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 91E(2) and the SEBI framework circular explicitly state that the AIR shall cover at least 67% of the program expenditure in the previous financial year. This lets the SIA focus the assurance effort on the material part of the program portfolio without requiring a 100% census. The Trap: 85% is the Section 11 application threshold for NPO income-tax exemption (Income-Tax Act) - a classic cross-regime confusion. 51% and 100% are distractors without regulatory basis in the SSE framework. Cross-Exam Context: V-A (MF Distributor) and X-A (Investment Adviser) both test the 85% Section 11 application rule for NPO taxation. XXIII tests the SSE-specific 67% AIR coverage rule. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When scoping the AIR, add the program-wise expenditure by descending spend till cumulative share crosses 67%. Document this cut-off in the engagement letter - so the audit trail shows you are NOT cherry-picking high-performing programs to satisfy the threshold.
